articles.title: Music Assistant offers to move Spotify to another speaker
articles.dek: Choose to stop the current player and start the music on the speaker you selected.
body: Music Assistant offers a choice when a Spotify account is already playing on another speaker: stop there and play here, or leave the existing music alone. The new dialog replaces a message that told the listener to stop the other player themselves.

For ordinary play or replace requests involving a track, album or playlist, the server checks before loading tracks or replacing the destination queue. That avoids waits of up to 45 seconds for a playlist that cannot start. The takeover choice appears only when the listener can control the other player.

Artist playback, shuffled selections and some queue actions are checked later, so they lack the same protection for the destination player. Retrying Play Now while keeping the queue can still add the requested items twice.

pullRequests.title: Offer to move Spotify playback here when another player holds it
Say at once that Spotify is busy elsewhere instead of after loading the playlist

articles.title: Home Assistant adds one-finger edge shortcuts on Android
articles.dek: Optional inward swipes can open the sidebar or run an existing gesture action, while Android navigation keeps priority.
body: Home Assistant’s Android app adds configurable one-finger swipes from the left and right edges of its page. Each can use an existing gesture action, including opening the sidebar, giving people another way to reach controls without using multiple fingers.

Both start with no action assigned. An option is hidden when Android reserves that edge for system navigation; its saved action is kept if the owner switches back to button navigation. Ordinary scrolling and touches away from the edges do not trigger the shortcut.
The addition is mmihaylov00’s first contribution to the Android app.

pullRequests.title: Add configurable one-finger edge swipe gestures

articles.title: Home Assistant’s infrared library adds commands for more appliances
articles.dek: Reusable command formats cover more air conditioners, fans and other equipment; integrations still need to adopt them.
body: Home Assistant’s infrared library adds command formats for a much wider range of household equipment. The work covers air-conditioner families from manufacturers including Mitsubishi, Hitachi, Toshiba, Midea and Panasonic, alongside television and audio formats, Dyson fans and Hob2Hood extractors.

The library can read more captured remote signals and preserve appliance-specific settings such as fan levels, presets and vane positions when constructing a command. It also handles some air-conditioner messages that a receiver splits into several captures.

Integrations still need to select the correct remote layout and translate its settings, and most devices need hardware validation. Paulus Schoutsen’s implementations are checked against reference signals and recorded packets; the library work does not itself add every listed appliance to Home Assistant.

pullRequests.title: Expand native infrared protocol and climate command coverage

articles.title: Sunshine Live brings 35 electronic-music channels to Music Assistant
articles.dek: The direct connection uses higher-quality streams without requiring an account.
body: Music Assistant adds a direct connection to Sunshine Live, the German electronic-music station and its 35 channels. It uses the station’s own 192 kbit/s MP3 streams rather than the 64 kbit/s main programme available through TuneIn, and needs no account.

The channel list comes from the station’s website, so new channels can appear automatically. Song titles follow the audio stream; during live shows, the provider uses the programme name instead of presenting “Simulcast” as a song. Jordi Böhme makes his first contribution to Music Assistant’s server with the provider.

articles.title: Deezer’s app follows listening in Music Assistant
articles.dek: An optional setting carries the queue and position back to Deezer when its app opens.
body: Music Assistant updates Deezer’s listening history as music starts, including albums, artists and playlists in the Deezer app’s recently played list. A new “Continue in the Deezer app” setting lets that app resume where Music Assistant stopped; it starts switched off.

The recent-listening view inside Music Assistant also refreshes every five minutes instead of every hour. Players that prepare a track before it starts can still put an unheard track into Deezer’s history.

pullRequests.title: Deezer: sync playback with the Deezer app

articles.title: Piper’s native library restores intelligible Tagalog speech
articles.dek: A sound-mapping error turned a tested voice into noise and could affect other voice configurations.
body: Applications using Piper’s native C++ speech library avoid a pronunciation-map error that turned a tested Tagalog voice into noise. The library treated some two-part vowel sounds as their first character, attaching extra sound identifiers to ordinary vowels.

Ihor Shevchuk separates those combinations from single sounds. Verification produced recognizable Tagalog speech and preserved the expected English output. Eighteen of the 206 checked voice configurations contain the affected kind of entry; applications need to adopt the library correction.

articles.title: Music Assistant reduces pauses during sound-based discovery
articles.dek: A large-library test shows severe recommendation requests no longer holding up the server for seconds.
body: Music Assistant reduces pauses caused by finding similar tracks in a large library. The affected searches could freeze the whole server, including music streams, while choosing a varied set of recommendations.

In Marcel van der Veldt’s 50,000-track test on an Apple Silicon Mac, a demanding request fell from a 17-second freeze to 12 milliseconds. It requested 100 tracks with five starting tracks, a search depth of five and diversity set to 0.2. Default similar-track settings stayed at two milliseconds; the selected tracks and their order stay the same.

pullRequests.title: Similar tracks and the Discover row no longer freeze the server on large libraries

articles.title: ESPHome restores pulse and input readings on RTL8720C devices
articles.dek: The Realtek chip keeps reporting signal changes instead of stopping after the first one.
body: ESPHome repairs pulse counting and interrupt-driven inputs on devices using the RTL8720C chip. Reading an input could disable the mechanism that reports its changes, leaving pulse counters at zero and binary sensors stuck after their first change.

J. Nick Koston makes those reads preserve the active interrupt. Tests on a BW15 board restored counting with the default pulse filter and kept a binary sensor following a changing signal. The correction is specific to RTL8720C; it does not resolve different pulse-counting limitations on RTL8710B or Beken chips.

pullRequests.title: [libretiny] Read pins in interrupts without detaching the interrupt on Realtek

articles.title: Lyon transit disruptions gain calendars in Home Assistant
articles.dek: Alerts are grouped by transit line and retain their start and end dates.
body: Home Assistant’s Grand Lyon data integration adds calendars for transit-network alerts. People can follow the alerts for a chosen line with their start and end dates.
The integration retrieves the network’s alerts together and presents them by line. It includes all alert kinds rather than choosing which disruptions deserve priority.

articles.title: Home Assistant shows the temperature BSB-LAN is actually targeting
articles.dek: Heating schedules and temporary overrides no longer leave the climate card showing the comfort setting throughout.
body: Home Assistant’s BSB-LAN climate control shows the temperature the heating controller is applying. It previously displayed the comfort setting even while an automatic schedule or room unit selected a different target.

In heating mode, changing the target adjusts the active comfort or reduced setting. In automatic or off mode, those temperatures must be edited through their separate number controls instead. Presets in automatic mode temporarily override the schedule; selecting automatic again ends the override.
The Comfort preset replaces None, and permanent reduced heating appears as Heat with the Eco preset. Controllers on the PPS bus no longer expose presets.

pullRequests.title: Show the active setpoint as the BSB-LAN climate target

articles.title: Home Assistant stops prolonging Homematic cloud blocks
articles.dek: Setup waits out the cloud service’s cooldown instead of repeatedly requesting the whole home.
body: Home Assistant waits when Homematic IP Cloud blocks an address for making too many requests. Previously, setup retried about every eighty seconds and downloaded the home’s state again, which could extend the block and keep the connection unavailable for hours.

The integration respects the fifteen-minute cooldown remembered after a rate-limit response and shows the remaining wait in its setup status. Installations that are not being throttled keep their existing behavior.

pullRequests.title: Wait out a HomematicIP Cloud throttle instead of retrying the setup against it

articles.title: Forecast.Solar’s library puts energy estimates in the right hour
articles.dek: Current-hour and next-hour calculations were each reading the preceding period.
body: Forecast.Solar’s Python library corrects hourly energy estimates that were shifted back by one period. Its current-hour value contained the previous hour’s energy, while the calculation used for Home Assistant’s next-hour sensor returned the current hour instead.

The correction follows the service’s timestamps, which mark the end of each measurement period. Tests cover hourly and fifteen-minute forecasts. It is Tagliax’s first contribution to the library; the separate remaining-energy-today calculation is unchanged.

pullRequests.title: Count energy values for the period that ends at their timestamp

articles.title: ESPHome reads light and weather measurements from GY-39 modules
articles.dek: One wired module supplies illuminance, temperature, humidity, pressure and altitude.
body: ESPHome adds support for the GY-39 environment module, giving makers five optional readings through one I²C connection: light level, temperature, humidity, pressure and altitude.

The driver reads the measurements together and handles temperatures below freezing and altitude below sea level. Stefan Kaps contributes the component and its configuration guide in his first contributions to ESPHome and its documentation.

articles.title: Music Assistant reads Deezer’s real audio quality before playback
articles.dek: High-resolution FLAC tracks avoid being reduced to CD quality inside the playback buffer.
body: Music Assistant checks a Deezer FLAC track’s actual sample rate and bit depth before playback. Deezer labels both CD-quality and higher-resolution files as FLAC, so the provider had declared every track as 44.1 kHz and 16-bit and reduced higher-quality audio before sending it on. This extends October’s format correction to Deezer’s provider-specific streams, which the earlier change excluded.

A test with a Sendspin player and USB audio converter preserved an 88.2 kHz, 24-bit track from its first play, while a CD-quality track remained at 44.1 kHz. The check is cached, and a failed format lookup leaves the previous playback path in place. Jean-Philippe Menil makes his first contribution to Music Assistant’s server with the correction.

pullRequests.title: Play Deezer hi-res tracks at their real sample rate and bit depth
